metadata.name: LOD Server Support
metadata.description: Voxy multiplayer support (unofficial). Enables players with Voxy to see fully rendered terrain out to hundreds of chunks on multiplayer servers without needing to explore the world first.

metadata:
name: LodServerSupport
version: '0.14.0'
main: dev.vox.lss.paper.LSSPaperPlugin
api-version: '26.2'
# DERIVED (R2-5): the value expands from `folia` membership in line.env's
# LINE_PAPER_LOADERS — the one per-line judgment ("does Folia exist upstream for
# THIS line?") lives there, beside the other line identity rows a fresh cut must
# touch anyway. Where true, Folia support is EXPERIMENTAL (single-player soak
# validated; concurrent multi-region ingress untested) — the flag is a loads-at-all
# statement, never a claim that SOAK_PLATFORM=folia has passed on this line.
folia-supported: true
# C5 (XVER §7): the Via mismatch guard reflectively reads ViaVersion's API when the
# plugin is present. softdepend keeps Spigot's classloader from logging the one-time
# "loaded class ... which is not a depend/softdepend" warning on the first handshake —
# noise that reads like an LSS bug. No hard dependency: without Via the probe is a
# silent no-signal. LibsDisguises (issue #282): the far-player privacy ladder reads
# DisguiseAPI reflectively to hide disguised players — same precedent (load ORDER +
# classloader visibility, never a hard depend; absent = the rung is skipped).
softdepend: [ViaVersion, LibsDisguises]
description: Voxy multiplayer support (unofficial). Enables players with Voxy to see fully rendered terrain out to hundreds of chunks on multiplayer servers without needing to explore the world first.
author: VoX
website: https://modrinth.com/plugin/lod-server-support
commands:
  lsslod:
    description: LOD Server Support admin commands
    usage: /lsslod <stats|diag|store|set|help>
    permission: lss.admin
permissions:
  lss.admin:
    description: Access to LSS admin commands
    default: op
  # Far players (v0.11.0 E1): server-side privacy lever — holders are never served as
  # far players regardless of the farPlayers mode (FARP §3.2). BOTH brand spellings are
  # declared (default false) and the enforcement honors either: Bukkit resolves an
  # UNDECLARED node to the op default, so a single-brand declaration plus a cross-brand
  # check would silently hide every op — and declaring both keeps the privacy grant
  # working across an LSS<->VSS jar swap.
  lss.farplayers.hidden:
    description: Players with this permission are never shown as far players
    default: false
  vss.farplayers.hidden:
    description: Players with this permission are never shown as far players (VSS spelling)
    default: false
  # Service gate (requireServicePermission, default false): with the config key on, only
  # holders are served LOD data — a handshake from anyone else is answered with an
  # enabled=false SessionConfig and no session. BOTH brand spellings are declared for the
  # reason spelled out on lss.farplayers.hidden above (Bukkit resolves an UNDECLARED node to
  # the op default, so a single-brand declaration plus a cross-brand check goes silently
  # wrong, and declaring both keeps grants alive across an LSS<->VSS jar swap).
  #
  # `default: true`, NOT op: everyone holds these unless an admin says otherwise, so arming
  # the gate on its own changes nothing for anybody — the original behavior, preserved. The
  # gate is a DENY tool: the only thing that takes LOD away is an explicit negative grant in
  # the permission plugin (e.g. LuckPerms `group default permission set lss.use false`).
  #
  # Enforcement requires BOTH spellings, so a negative grant on EITHER one denies — the De
  # Morgan mirror of the privacy nodes above (grant model: hold EITHER; deny model: lose
  # EITHER). An OR here would be inert: the spelling the admin did NOT touch still resolves
  # to its declared `true` and would out-vote the single negative grant.
  #
  # That direction is also why losing either declaration is dangerous: an undeclared node
  # falls back to Bukkit's op default, silently turning "everyone" into "ops only".
  lss.use:
    description: Receive LOD data when requireServicePermission is enabled
    default: true
  vss.use:
    description: Receive LOD data when requireServicePermission is enabled (VSS spelling)
    default: true

modLoader="javafml"
loaderVersion="[4,)"
license="MIT"
issueTrackerURL="https://github.com/VoX/lod-server-support/issues"

[[mods]]
modId="lss"
version="0.14.0"
displayName="LOD Server Support"
authors="VoX"
logoFile="assets/lss/icon.png"
description='''Voxy multiplayer support (unofficial). Enables players with Voxy to see fully rendered terrain out to hundreds of chunks on multiplayer servers without needing to explore the world first. Server-side works with any LSS/VSS client; the client half needs a community Voxy build for NeoForge.'''

[[mixins]]
config="lss.neoforge.mixins.json"

[[mixins]]
config="lss-sodium-legacy.mixins.json"

[[dependencies.lss]]
    modId="neoforge"
    type="required"
    # DERIVED (R2-6): the loader floor is neoforge_version's first two components
    # (26.2.0.59 -> [26.2,)) — the hand row churned on all three v0.11 ports.
    versionRange="[26.2,)"
    ordering="NONE"
    side="BOTH"

[[dependencies.lss]]
    modId="minecraft"
    type="required"
    versionRange="[26.2]"
    ordering="NONE"
    side="BOTH"

# Sodium 0.8+ options page (sodium-options-page-generations-plan.md, NeoForge
# amendment): sodium-neoforge's ConfigLoaderForge reads this property from every
# mod and instantiates the named ConfigEntryPoint — the same key Fabric declares
# as an entrypoint. Harmless when Sodium is absent or pre-0.8.
[modproperties.lss]
"sodium:config_api_user"="dev.vox.lss.config.LSSConfigMenu"

  # Far players (v0.11.0 E1): server-side privacy lever — holders are never served as
  # far players regardless of the farPlayers mode (FARP §3.2). BOTH brand spellings are
  # declared (default false) and the enforcement honors either: Bukkit resolves an
  # UNDECLARED node to the op default, so a single-brand declaration plus a cross-brand
  # check would silently hide every op — and declaring both keeps the privacy grant
  # working across an LSS<->VSS jar swap.
  lss.farplayers.hidden:
    description: Players with this permission are never shown as far players
    default: false
  vss.farplayers.hidden:
    description: Players with this permission are never shown as far players (VSS spelling)
    default: false
  # Service gate (requireServicePermission, default false): with the config key on, only
  # holders are served LOD data — a handshake from anyone else is answered with an
  # enabled=false SessionConfig and no session. BOTH brand spellings are declared for the
  # reason spelled out on lss.farplayers.hidden above (Bukkit resolves an UNDECLARED node to
  # the op default, so a single-brand declaration plus a cross-brand check goes silently
  # wrong, and declaring both keeps grants alive across an LSS<->VSS jar swap).
  #
  # `default: true`, NOT op: everyone holds these unless an admin says otherwise, so arming
  # the gate on its own changes nothing for anybody — the original behavior, preserved. The
  # gate is a DENY tool: the only thing that takes LOD away is an explicit negative grant in
  # the permission plugin (e.g. LuckPerms `group default permission set lss.use false`).
  #
  # Enforcement requires BOTH spellings, so a negative grant on EITHER one denies — the De
  # Morgan mirror of the privacy nodes above (grant model: hold EITHER; deny model: lose
  # EITHER). An OR here would be inert: the spelling the admin did NOT touch still resolves
  # to its declared `true` and would out-vote the single negative grant.
  #
  # That direction is also why losing either declaration is dangerous: an undeclared node
  # falls back to Bukkit's op default, silently turning "everyone" into "ops only".
  lss.use:
    description: Receive LOD data when requireServicePermission is enabled
    default: true
  vss.use:
    description: Receive LOD data when requireServicePermission is enabled (VSS spelling)
    default: true
